name: Heyo
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only survey/comparative items (Laycock 1968, Hutchinson 1981); no grammar or phonology of Heyo located.

sources.citation: University at Buffalo Linguistics doctoral alumni list (2019-2024) and M. S. Dryer's 'Downloadable student dissertations' page (acsu.buffalo.edu/~dryer/dissertations.htm).
sources.note: No dissertation by Thomas Diaz and none on Heyo is listed (Torricelli items are Wilson 2017 Yeri and Drinfeld 2024 Aro); Diaz's Heyo grammar is therefore still unpublished as far as these lists show.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2006. Torricelli languages. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language & Linguistics, 2nd ed. Elsevier. doi:10.1016/b0-08-044854-2/04600-9
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only: 'although stress is frequently contrastive, reports of tonal differences are rare'; nothing specific to Heyo.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid heyo1240 and reference records 68747 (Jore, Lambrecht, Troolin & Wise 2002, 'Sociolinguistic survey of the Heyo language', SIL-PNG, 65 pp., no URL), 131770 (Hutchinson 1981, sil_id 15997), 138610 (Laycock 1968, Heyo p.48, listed by Glottolog as an overview/comparative/wordlist).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 0 grammar/phonology/sketch refs; Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist (Laycock 1968).

sources.citation: Diaz, Thomas (collector). 2018-2019. Heyo elicitation and wordlist recordings: 'Susan explains words in Heyo' (heyo003), 'Elicitation on basic clauses / adjectives / nominal phrase', 'Clause linkage' (heyo087); plus the NSF-era Heyo deposit at PARADISEC.
sources.note: Audio with ELAN transcriptions from which stress placement could be measured directly if no written statement is obtainable.

sources.citation: ELAR collection 0550 (ELDP IGS0344), 'Documentation of Heyo [auk], a Torricelli language of Papua New Guinea', depositor Thomas Diaz (University at Buffalo), 2018-2020, hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-0012-57CA-D; collection description and item pages 1, 5-10 of 10.
sources.note: Nothing. Description notes gender marking by affixation/clitics, triple negation, 'no standardized orthography' (y=[j], '=[ʔ]); 'reference grammar' listed as forthcoming but not deposited. Written items are only 'HeyoOrthography' (login-restricted: 'This file cannot be displayed.. you do not have permission'), 'FLEx backup of Heyo data', and elicitation audio (Clause linkage 2019, adjectives, basic clauses, nominal phrase, 'Susan explains words in Heyo' 2018).

sources.citation: NSF award 1826767 (2018-2020), 'Doctoral Dissertation Grant: Documentation and Analysis of a Typologically Uncommon Maimai Language', PI Matthew S. Dryer, co-PI Thomas Diaz, SUNY Buffalo; abstract + project outcomes report (modified 2020-11-06 by T. Diaz).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Confirms Heyo/Maimai 'remains completely undocumented' before the project; outcomes: ~40 h recordings archived at ELAR; 'a dictionary of Heyo, a grammatical description of the language, and a pedagogical grammar.. begun, but have not been completed as of July 2020'.

sources.citation: Hutchinson, Ian. 1981. A sociolinguistic survey of Heyo, Pahi and Mayo-Pasi. In Richard Loving (ed.), Sociolinguistic surveys of Sepik languages (Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 29), 109-140. Ukarumpa: SIL. (SIL archives 23824; image-only scan, scanned 300 dpi)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/phonolog/phonem/syllab returns no hits; Heyo sections read: p.113 'No linguistic work has been done on any of the other three languages' (Heyo, Pahi, Pasi) and speakers 'prefer their language to be called Wanib'; p.125 all six Heyo villages claim no dialects; pp.127-128 lexicostatistics (Heyo villages 84-96%, Heyo 3% with Mayo/Pasi/Pahi); p.130 closest languages Yahang and Siliput; p.131 allocation site Yimut-Ulap; p.140 Heyo village names. No phonology, no wordlist printed.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1 (PL C-38), 767-782. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.767
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; general Torricelli phonology paragraph (places of articulation, vowels, fricatives) only; Heyo appears solely in the Maimai Family census list (1872).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification (Pacific Linguistics B-25). Canberra: ANU. Entry 36 HEYO (Arinwa, Lolopani, Ruruhip, Wanwan), 1872 speakers.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; village index and population only.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Heyo' (38 lexical items from Laycock 1968) and Wikipedia 'Heyo language' (stub) / 'Maimai languages' (pronouns ai/is/apan/apap and 25-item vocabulary after Foley 2018 and Laycock 1968).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only; no stress or accent marks on any Heyo form; no prose on phonology.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (Maimai section, pp. ~316 ff. in the e-book).

sources.citation: Jore, Tim, Philip Lambrecht, Dave Troolin & Rob Wise. 2002. Sociolinguistic survey of the Heyo language. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG survey report, 65 pp.

sources.note: Longest Heyo-specific document; SIL-PNG 2002 surveys usually append 170-item phonetic wordlists that show stress marking, and occasionally a phonology note.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1968. Languages of the Lumi Subdistrict (West Sepik District), New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 7(1): 36-66 (Heyo section p.48; wordlist and transcription conventions).

sources.note: Only published first-hand Heyo data (Laycock's 1967 survey); his per-language notes sometimes include a one-line remark on stress, and the introduction states what his accent marks mean.

sources.citation: Diaz, Thomas. in preparation. A grammar of Heyo (Wanib), a Maimai (Torricelli) language of Papua New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University at Buffalo (SUNY), advisor Matthew S. Dryer; NSF DDRIG 1826767, ELDP IGS0344.
